capabilities: Run JMESPath expressions on a JSON or JSONL vault file
Display array results as tables and copy the full result as JSON
Save and reuse named query pairs
Run a saved query across up to 20 chosen files (Pro)
Write query results as CSV or Markdown report files (Pro)
disambiguation: Not JSONPath despite the plugin ID; it supports JMESPath expressions only.
extras: Freemium: core query features are free; multi-file runs and report writing require a paid GitHub Sponsors sponsorship, verified via GitHub device-flow sign-in that only checks sponsorship status and sends no vault data. The settings open a 'What's new' tab promoting other NoteMods plugins and Zovo Chat. The README lists untested areas (mobile, Linux desktop, real clipboard writes, real sponsorship checks).
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to run structured queries against JSON or JSONL data files stored in the vault.

relations.evidence: The query runs on your device with bundled jmespath.js 0.16.0.

requires.name: GitHub Sponsors sponsorship of theluckystrike ($5/month or $15 once)

summary: JMESPath query view that runs local queries on JSON and JSONL files in the vault and shows results as tables, scalars, or copied JSON.
